Chapter 10. The Long Shadow of Climate.
Have you ever noticed how the air just feels different when everything goes quiet—when the engines stop running? For centuries, our world was shaped by the burning of coal, oil, and gas. All that carbon we sent up, warming the planet, shifting the weather... it changed everything.
Now, imagine a world without us. No more emissions pouring into the sky. Sounds peaceful, right? But the effects of our choices don’t just vanish overnight.
Picture a climate scientist, looking back from some future vantage point. They’d see our influence slowly unwinding—carbon dioxide levels dropping, but oh so gradually. The oceans do their part, pulling in some of the excess. Forests, left to grow wild and free, soak up even more.
Over decades... centuries, really, the climate begins to settle down. But the marks we left? They stick around. Glaciers keep melting. Sea levels have risen—and they don’t just fall back. Rain and drought patterns are all mixed up, still shifting in the aftermath.
And here’s something we can’t ignore. Some changes just can’t be undone. Islands swallowed by the sea? They stay gone. Species we lost forever? They don’t come back. Yet, the world moves forward. New ecosystems pop up, shaped by both the warming we left behind and our sudden absence.
The story of climate is really about loss and renewal, all tangled together. Most days, we don’t notice these shifts—at least, not right away. But in a world without us, the message is clear: our collective actions have incredible power. And the costs of doing nothing? They cast a long shadow.
